title: openai-compat: tool_choice semantics + schema mapping + tool message formatting
author: Lena Mfcller
description:
Motivation: Align Redwood's OpenAI-compatibility layer with evolving function/tool-calling semantics adopted by downstream SDKs and partners. This PR implements three closely-related features: 1) tool_choice semantics for multi-tool selection and disambiguation, 2) a flexible tool schema mapping layer that translates OpenAI-style JSON schema/tool descriptors to our internal ToolSpec, and 3) deterministic tool message formatting for logs, streaming payloads, and telemetry.

Summary of changes (high-level):
- Add `tool_choice` handling to the compat layer so responses that choose a tool are surfaced as a single canonical event instead of ad-hoc messages; preserve original OpenAI fields for telemetry.
- Implement schema mapping utilities: map OpenAI `functions` schema into internal `ToolSpec` (types, required fields, JSON schema -> internal field descriptors, enum handling). Support partial schemas and fallback heuristics.
- Normalize tool invocation messages used in streaming (first event), sync responses (function_call object), and in internal audit logs to a single canonical text format to avoid parser drift across consumers.
- Update runtime routing code so that tool-invocation decisions can be routed to Dedicated/private tool runners and includes versioned tool ids.
- Tests: unit tests for mapping edge cases (oneOf, nullable, arrays), integration tests exercising a simple tool round-trip via the OpenAI compatibility API, and an end-to-end test using the SDK example.

Compatibility and migration notes:
- Backwards compatible: default behavior is unchanged for callers that receive raw messages. New `tool_choice` is emitted as an explicit top-level event in streaming protocols and as `tool_choice` field on the compat response for non-streaming calls. Consumers that relied on parsing raw assistant messages should add a fallback to inspect `tool_choice` when present.
- For private deployments, operators can opt-out of schema mapping by setting `compat.openai.disable_schema_mapping=true` in config (added in this PR).

Implementation details (commits below):
- New package `redwood-openai-compat/tooling` with `schema_mapper.go` and `tool_choice.go` (Go, shared by runtime and API gateway).
- Changes to `api/streaming` to emit deterministic tool invocation event as the first event in a tool call stream. Also adjusts the event envelope to include `tool_version` and `mapped_schema_v` metadata.
- Small changes in `sdk-typescript` examples to show how to inspect `tool_choice` both in streaming and non-streaming flows.

Test plan: CI unit/integration suite + manual verification using `examples/tool-call-demo` tested in staging (deployed behind dedicated gateway). Load test with the perf-canary to ensure no regression in median latency; observed ~0.6% median token latency increase in dev runs (within SLO).

Risks and mitigations:
- Schema mapping is heuristic: added conservative defaults and clear logs when mapping fails. Mismapped types fall back to raw JSON schema to avoid silent corruption.
- Streaming change may break some SDK consumers if they assumed message ordering; documented the new event envelope and added feature flag for backwards compatibility in the gateway.

Files changed (high-level): `redwood-openai-compat/*`, `api/streaming/*`, `runtime/toolrouter/*`, `sdk-typescript/examples/*`, `infra/config/compat.yml`, `test/integration/tooling_test.go`.

Related Linear tasks: ENG-2304 (tooling compat), PM-112 (openai compat roadmap).

release_notes: OpenAI compatibility: new tool_choice event emitted for tool selections in streaming and non-streaming flows.
Schema mapping: OpenAI `functions` schemas are now translated into internal ToolSpec with conservative fallbacks for unknown types.
Deterministic tool message formatting for streaming/audit logs to reduce parsing differences across SDKs.
